# Working on prompt-library-site

prompt-library-site is built on **vanilla-mvc**: MVC, an event bus, and change that is *stated*, never detected.
It is not React, Vue, Svelte or lit, and the habits from those are the mistakes here. Read this
before writing code.

## The one that compiles and does nothing

A DOM handler is registered in the controller, then bound **by name** in the template:

```ts
// controller
protected override onInterconnect(): void {
  this.handle('save', this.#save);
}
#save(): void {
  this.domain.notes.save(this.model.draft);   // a gesture goes to the application domain
}

// template
html`<button @click=${c.handler('save')}>Save</button>`
```

Never `@click=${() => c.save()}`. The framework refuses it when the template is built, with a
TypeError that says this. `prevent()`, `field()`, `formValues()` and `keys()` keep the registration
of the handler they wrap.

## The loop every feature is

1. A **gesture** — a registered DOM handler — calls a **capability** on the application domain.
2. The capability changes what it owns and **publishes a fact**: an event, plain data.
3. A controller **subscribed** to that fact maps it onto its **model** and calls `this.changed()`.
4. The gesture ends; the framework draws everything that said it changed, once.

A handler never writes the model. A model write nobody states with `changed()` is never drawn.
Work that waits (a promise) is returned from the handler, or handed to `this.own()`.

## Where things go

| Thing | Where | Make it with |
|---|---|---|
| A component | `src/components/<name>/`: `.model.ts` (types only), `.controller.ts`, `.template.ts`, `.component.ts`, `.style.ts` | `npx vanilla-mvc add component <name>` |
| An event | `src/events/<name>.ts`: one interface, `readonly type` equal to its name | `npx vanilla-mvc add event <Name>` |
| A capability | `src/application/<name>.ts`, adopted in `ApplicationDomain.onCreate` with `this.adopt(…)` | `npx vanilla-mvc add capability <name>` |

Use the generators. They write the shape the rules below check for.

## Before you say it is done

`npm test` — it runs `test/architecture.test.mjs`, which checks every rule below over `src/`.
A red rule names the file and line.

## The rules

1. **Import only the framework package and your own source.** Anything else is a dependency the architecture never agreed to. The framework has no runtime dependencies so an application can have few too.
2. **Reach the router, fields and templates libraries through the framework's seams, never directly. Style and template files may import vanilla-mvc/css.** The seams are what let a library be swapped. A component that imports RouteTable has welded itself to one router.
3. **Take `css`, `Style` and `styled` from 'vanilla-mvc'. The css library lends engines (layout, theme…), not its tag.** The framework's css tag goes through the styling seam, which owns the sheet. The library's raw tag bypasses it.
4. **Only a controller imports from application/. Models, templates and styles see only their own component.** The controller is the one place presentation meets the application. A template that reaches the domain has two masters.
5. **An event file imports only other event files.** Events are the contract between the application and presentation. A contract that imports one side belongs to it.
6. **Nothing under application/ imports from components/.** The application domain knows nothing about screens. It publishes facts; whoever cares maps them.
7. **A *.model.ts lives in its component folder and holds types only: interfaces, type aliases, type-only imports.** The model is what the view reads. The moment it holds behaviour, the view has somewhere to put logic.
8. **One event per file under events/, exported as an interface or a type — never a class.** An event is plain frozen data on the bus. A class invites methods, and a second event in the file hides from the one looking for it.
9. **An event interface's `type` is the string of its own name.** Subscribers key on the string. A mismatch compiles, and the subscriber never hears the event.
10. **Register every handler as a private method — this.handle(name, this.#method), this.subscribe(type, this.#method) — and give a controller no public member of its own.** A controller is driven by gestures and facts, not by callers. A public method is an invitation to call it from somewhere the change engine cannot see.
11. **Whatever writes the model — the handler, or any method it calls — must reach this.changed().** There is no change detection. A write nobody states is never drawn.
12. **A promise a controller starts is returned, awaited, or handed to this.own().** A DOM event is one synchronous stack. A promise leaves it, and whatever it publishes when it settles has no gesture to end — so nothing draws it unless its starter owns it.
13. **Write the css tag inside the Style callback, never at the top of a module.** The tag goes through the styling adapter, which Application.create() installs. At import there is none, and the whole application fails to boot with 'No adapters installed.'
14. **A DOM handler calls the application domain and writes nothing. The model changes when the fact comes back.** If the click writes the model, the domain never hears of it — and the next screen that cares has no fact to hear.
15. **Add a child with this.adopt(capability), never this.children.push(capability).** push() alone compiles and runs until the child publishes. Then it fails somewhere else as 'not attached to an application', because the bus is found through parent.
16. **A controller never calls changes.update(). It states changes; the gesture ends the pass.** One gesture, one render. A controller that renders mid-gesture draws a half-updated screen, and draws it twice.

Wrong and right for each: `npx vanilla-mvc rules`.
